raw_response:
I have farmed for a long time, and with only 9 mu I do not want to spread myself too thin or take big risks. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I will keep the plan simple and manageable with the labor I can count on at home. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield when the rains are not enough, but I still will not overdo water because pumping costs money. I grow cotton, maize, and wheat, and because cotton is my main system, I will give the largest share of land to cotton and keep smaller areas for wheat and maize so I still have grain and cash income together. I will use better seed where it helps me most, keep fertilizer at moderate levels, spray when needed to avoid serious pest loss, and use the kind of tillage I can manage reliably with the equipment and habits I already know. My goal is steady production and lower risk, not chasing the highest possible yield.
